**Zhejiang University** (**ZJU**) is a [public university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university") in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), Zhejiang, China. It is affiliated with the [Ministry of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_\(China\) "Ministry of Education \(China\)"). The university is part of [Project 211](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_211 "Project 211"), [Project 985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_985 "Project 985"), and [Double First-Class Construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_First-Class_Construction "Double First-Class Construction").
The university was established as **National Third Chung Shan University**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-zhongshan-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-6) in 1927, in memory of Sun Yat-sen, and soon renamed as **National Chekiang University**[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-9) (**NCKU**) in 1928.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-zju-history-10) During the presidency of [Chu Kochen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Coching "Chu Coching") from 1936 to 1949, the university retreated to [Guizhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guizhou "Guizhou") in Western China during the [Second Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War"),[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:31-11) before it moved back to Hangzhou in 1946. After the [Communist Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Revolution "Chinese Communist Revolution"), the university was [re-organized as an engineering-specialized university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_reorganisation_of_Chinese_higher_education "1952 reorganisation of Chinese higher education") in 1952. In 1998, [Zhejiang Medical University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Medical_University "Zhejiang Medical University"), [Hangzhou University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_University "Hangzhou University") and [Zhejiang Agricultural University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_Agricultural_University "Zhejiang Agricultural University"), which were derived from former departments of ZJU, merged and formed the present-day ZJU as a comprehensive university.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:5-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:7-13)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:6-8)
The university maintains seven faculties with 37 colleges and schools, offering about 140 undergraduate and 300 graduate programs.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-Study_at_Zhejiang_University-14) The university also has seven affiliated hospitals, one museum, and two international joint institutes.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-Zhejiang_University_Facts_and_Figures-15) Fifty-two members of ZJU faculty are also members of the [Chinese Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Sciences "Chinese Academy of Sciences") or the [Chinese Academy of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Engineering "Chinese Academy of Engineering").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:3-16) The university is a member of the [C9 League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C9_League "C9 League").
Zhejiang University was ranked first worldwide among academic institutions for scientific research output by the [Nature Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nature_Index "Nature Index") in 2026 and the [CWTS Leiden Ranking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CWTS_Leiden_Ranking "CWTS Leiden Ranking") Traditional Edition in 2025.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:2-18) Notable alumni of the university include Chinese premier [Li Qiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Li_Qiang "Li Qiang"), entrepreneurs [Duan Yongping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duan_Yongping "Duan Yongping") and [Colin Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Huang "Colin Huang"), and [DeepSeek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek "DeepSeek") founder [Liang Wenfeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liang_Wenfeng "Liang Wenfeng").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-Brookings_Institution-19)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:0-20)
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
### 1897–1914: college-preparatory school
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1897–1914: college-preparatory school")]
See also: [Qiushi Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiushi_Academy "Qiushi Academy") and [Puci Temple (Hangzhou)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puci_Temple_\(Hangzhou\) "Puci Temple \(Hangzhou\)")
Established in 1897 by Hangzhou's mayor, Lin Qi, Qiushi Academy was the major predecessor to the university.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-zju-history-10) The educational reforms of 1902 and 1904 in China led to the academy being renamed Chekiang University in 1902,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-21) and subsequently Chekiang Higher Institute in 1903.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-22) Elmer L. Mattox of [Hangchow Presbyterian College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangchow_University "Hangchow University") was appointed as the head teacher of the college, responsible for supervising and organising teaching. The Institute was the first provincial educational institution to send students to study abroad.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:17-23)
However, the proposed reforms under the new republican government following the 1911 revolution sparked controversy, causing the Institutes to cease student recruitment in 1912 and ultimately close in 1914.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-24)
In 1947, [Chang Ch'i-yun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chang_Ch'i-yun "Chang Ch'i-yun"), a professor at NCKU, began attributing the university's origin to the Qiushi Academy, which was later acknowledge in the yearbook of the [Ministry of Education of the Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_of_the_Republic_of_China "Ministry of Education of the Republic of China").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:4-25)
### 1928–1949: national university
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1928–1949: national university")]
After the closure of Cheking Higher Institute, the attempts to restore the institute was unsuccessful due to conflicts between warlords.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:52-26) After the Northern Expedition in July 1927, the [Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuomintang "Kuomintang") (KMT) took control of Hangzhou and established the National Third Chungshan University,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:19-27) by merging Chekiang Industrial College and Chekiang Agricultural College on the original site of Qiushi Academy.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:52-26) On April 1, 1928, the institution was renamed Chekiang University, and later that year it was renamed National Chekiang University (NCKU),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:52-26) with [Jiang Menglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiang_Menglin "Jiang Menglin"), an alumnus and teacher of Qiushi, as its first president.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:7-13)
In 1929, Jiang was succeeded by [Shao Peizi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shao_Peizi "Shao Peizi"), also an alumnus and teacher of Qiushi.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:62-28) Shao refused to join KMT, which led to a tense relationship between the university and the government, and the government withdrew funding in 1932, leading to Shao's resignation. [Cheng Tien-fong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheng_Tien-fong "Cheng Tien-fong"), a member of the KMT, was then appointed by the [Nationalist government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nationalist_government "Nationalist government") as the new president. Under his leadership, with the personal intervention of [Chiang Kai-shek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiang_Kai-shek "Chiang Kai-shek"), the university began to receive direct funding from the central government.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:62-28)
In March 1933, [Kuo Zing-Yang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zing-Yang_Kuo "Zing-Yang Kuo"), another KMT member, became president. But as the Sino-Japanese conflict intensified and the Nationalist government's response to the invasion was perceived as lenient, its popularity waned. This discontent culminated in the December 9 Movement of 1935, when students ousted Kuo from office, accusing him of collaborating with the police to arrest student demonstrators.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-29)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:62-28)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Zhu_Kezhen_01.jpg/250px-Zhu_Kezhen_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zhu_Kezhen_01.jpg)[Chu Kochen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Coching "Chu Coching"), president of National Chekiang University from 1936–1949
[Chu Kochen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Coching "Chu Coching"), a scholar with no previous political appointments, was recommended to Chiang Kai-shek by Chen Bulei for the presidency of NCKU in April 1936. Kochen's inauguration was presided over by [Jiang Menglin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiang_Menglin "Jiang Menglin").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-30) Backed by Chen Bulei's strong financial backing and authority to make political appointments within the university, Chu was able to attract leading members of the [Science Society of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_Society_of_China "Science Society of China") and the [_Critical Review_ Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_Review_Group?action=edit&redlink=1 "Critical Review Group \(page does not exist\)").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-31) In the second half of 1937, with the outbreak of the [Second Sino-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Sino-Japanese_War "Second Sino-Japanese War") and the advance of the Japanese army, the university was forced to move from Hangzhou, first to Yishan, then to Zunyi, and finally to Meitan in [Guizhou Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guizhou "Guizhou") in southwest China. During this period, the students of NCKU took on the responsibility of safeguarding Zhejiang's historical collections, including the [_Complete Library of the Four Treasuries_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siku_Quanshu "Siku Quanshu") housed in the [Wenlan Pavilion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenlan_Pavilion "Wenlan Pavilion"), to prevent their capture by Japanese forces.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:8-32)
In March 1945, Fei Gong, an NCKU professor and critic of the Nationalist government, disappeared in Chongqing in what was later proved to be a government assassination.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:9-33) In September, with the surrender of Japan, a group of NCKU professors led by [Luo Zongluo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Tsung-lo "Lo Tsung-lo") were ordered by the government to take over the Japanese [Imperial University in Taiwan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Taiwan_University "National Taiwan University").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:9-33) In October, the students and faculty who had retreated to Longquan began to return to Hangzhou, while those who had retreated to Guizhou returned in May 1946 with the help of the [United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Relief_and_Rehabilitation_Administration "United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration"). The university set up its first medical school on the instructions of the Ministry of Education.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:9-33)
In late 1947, [the death of Yu Zisan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yu_Zisan_Incident "Yu Zisan Incident"), the president of the university's student union, led to strikes and protests. While Chu attempted to strike a balance between his students and the Nationalist government, his relationship with the students worsened and he moved to Shanghai, upon the request of the Nationalist government. But he eventually did not move to Taiwan and secretly stayed at the [Academia Sinica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academia_Sinica "Academia Sinica") building in Shanghai, until the Communist takeover of the NCKU campus in May 1949.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:10-34)
### 1949–1976: Mao Zedong era
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1949–1976: Mao Zedong era")]
In August 1948, [Ma Yinchu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ma_Yinchu "Ma Yinchu") was appointed as the university president, who promoted communist education and organisations within the university.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:122-35) In 1950, the new Ministry of Education instructed all universities to remove "National" from their names. Hence the university's name was changed to its present name in Chinese, or Zhejiang University (ZJU). The communist education among faculty evolved into the [Thought Reform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thought_reform_in_China "Thought reform in China") and [Three-anti and Five-anti Campaigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-anti_and_Five-anti_Campaigns "Three-anti and Five-anti Campaigns") after Ma was appointed the president of [Peking University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peking_University "Peking University") in 1949.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:122-35) ZJU scholars such as [Su Buqing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Su_Buqing "Su Buqing"), [Tan Jiazhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tan_Jiazhen "Tan Jiazhen"), [Wang Guosong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Guosong "Wang Guosong") became targets of political prosecution.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-36)
In the early 1950s, the university underwent [a series of re-organisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_reorganisation_of_Chinese_higher_education "1952 reorganisation of Chinese higher education"), which aimed to establish a Soviet-styled education system, to eventually became an engineering-focused university., which only had the departments of electrical engineering, chemical engineering, civil engineering and mechanical engineering. The engineering school of Hangchow University merged into ZJU. The university's College of Agriculture became an independent university, named Zhejiang Agricultural University. The university's medical school merged into Zhejiang Provincial Medical College to become Zhejiang Medical College.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:02-37) The departments of Chinese Literature, Foreign Literature and Education was merged into Zhejiang Teachers College and relocated to the campus of Hangchow University.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:22-38) The faculty of College of Sciences were sent to Chinese Academy of Sciences.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-39)
In 1954, the university moved from Daxue Road to Yuquan.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-40) Liu Dan, the university's [Party Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party_Committee_Secretary "Chinese Communist Party Committee Secretary"), restored sciences research and education as part of the university's engineering offerings.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:310-41) In 1963, ZJU was selected as one of the National Key Universities.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-42)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/65/Yuquan_campus_4.jpg/330px-Yuquan_campus_4.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yuquan_campus_4.jpg)A statue of [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") was set up at the Zhejiang University campus on December 26, 1969 as a result of [Mao Zedong's cult of personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong's_cult_of_personality "Mao Zedong's cult of personality") during the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution"). The statue remains a major landmark at [Yuquan Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuquan_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Yuquan Campus, Zhejiang University").
In 1966, the Cultural Revolution broke out and the university ceased to function. Liu Dan was removed from office after being attacked by the _Zhejiang Daily_ and the _People's Daily_. There was an emergence of radical groups in favour of Cultural Revolution._[[ 41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-43)_ In August, the ZJU students confronted with younger [red guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Guards "Red Guards"), who were mostly high school students, to protect [Lingyin Temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingyin_Temple "Lingyin Temple") from their attempts to destroy [Four Olds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Olds "Four Olds").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-44) In 1967, at a meeting with [Tan Zhenlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tan_Zhenlin "Tan Zhenlin") in Beijing, red guards from ZJU were told that [Mao Zedong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong") wanted to protect [Jiang Hua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiang_Hua "Jiang Hua") in this revolution. This led to a split within red guards in Zhejiang, particularly with another faction led by Zhang Yongsheng from the Chinese Academy of Art, who wanted to persecute Jiang Hua. The two factions fought each other constantly throughout the Cultural Revolution.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:132-45)
### 1976 to present
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1976 to present")]
With the end of the [Cultural Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution") in 1976, Liu returned to ZJU as the honorary president, the only by far.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:310-41) In November 1980, ZJU became co-funded by both Ministry of Education and Zhejiang's provincial government.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In 1989, Zhejiang University students, along with more than 10 other universities in Hangzhou, demonstrated in Wulin Square in support of the democracy movement in Beijing. After hearing of the massacre in Beijing, the student protesters blocked the railway at Nanxingqiao station with their bodies for three days before negotiating with the vice-governor, Chai Songyue. At least 60 passenger trains and 166 freight trains were blocked during the protest.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:27-46)
Since 1988 to 1995, Lu Yongxiang assumed the president of Zhejiang University, during which he made "pursuing innovation" part of the university motto and reformed teaching and research systems, including introduction of the program of Advanced Honor Class of Engineering Education.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In 1995, it was selected into Project 211.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-47) In 1997, Wang Ganchang and Bei Shizhang in Beijing, and Su Buqing and Tan Jiazhen in Shanghai, wrote a joint letter to the then General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party, Jiang Zemin, recommending a merger of the four universities.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:02-37): 94  In 1998, with the approval of the State Council, the new Zhejiang University was established as a merger of four major universities.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:7-13) With over 30,000 students and 10,000 staff, the new Zhejiang University was considered the largest higher education institution in Asia.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-48) Zhang Junsheng was appointed Party secretary of the university to oversee the merger.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-49) In 2005, the university founded Zhejiang University Holding Group, later renamed as Zhejiang University Yuanzheng Holding Group. As of 2022, there are several companies affiliated to the group have been publicly listed, including Insigma Technology, United Mechanical & Electrical, and Shenghua Land.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-%E4%BB%8B%E7%BB%8D-50) In October 2005, the university's Hubin campus was sold at the price of 2.46 billion Chinese yuan to [Kerry Properties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerry_Properties "Kerry Properties") for commercial complex development.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-%E6%8B%8D%E5%87%BA-51) In June 2012, Zhejiang University founded the Ocean College in collaboration with [Zhoushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhoushan "Zhoushan") municipal government.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-52)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-53)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-54) In December 2014, the university signed an agreement with the [University of Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh "University of Edinburgh") to form [a joint institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University-University_of_Edinburgh_Institute "Zhejiang University-University of Edinburgh Institute") at the Haining campus.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-55) In July 2015, another agreement to build a joint institute was signed with the [University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Illinois_Urbana-Champaign "University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-56) In September 2016, the new Haining campus came into use.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:15-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:16-58)
In April 2013, 53 alumni co-signed a petition against the appointment of [Lin Jianhua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin_Jianhua "Lin Jianhua") as Zhejiang University's new president. An open letter by the alumni says, "Zhejiang University needs an upright and capable academic leader, not a mediocre chief executive."[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-59) In November 2013, Chu Jian, vice president of the university who was rumoured to be behind the rare petition, was arrested for bribery,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-n-60) yet he was not tried until 2017 and was soon released after he was sentenced to 3 years in jail which had almost been fulfilled by the time of trial.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-61)
In September 2013, amid extensive objection from local residents and university alumni, part of Huajiachi campus was sold at the price of 13.67 billion Chinese yuan, making the land the most expensive in the city's history.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:29-62)
In July 2020, the university [came under intense criticism for allowing an ethnic minority student convicted of rape to remain enrolled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Zhejiang_University_rapes "2019 Zhejiang University rapes").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-63)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:25-64)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-65) The public questioned whether the university's decision was too lenient for sexual harassments.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-66)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:25-64) The overwhelming public opinions made the university review the case, and eventually expelled the student.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-67)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-68)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-69)
In November 2020, the university founded its new Ningbo campus.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-70) In 2019, the Institute of Hainan were founded in [Sanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanya "Sanya"), Hainan. In 2021, new institutes were founded in Quzhou, Jinhua, Wenzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, Shaoxing and Taizhou within Zhejiang. In March 2021, tech tycoon [Colin Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Huang "Colin Huang") donated $100 million to support the university's Shanghai Institute for Advanced Study.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-71)

### Current campuses
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Current campuses")]
With seven campuses, namely Zijingang, Yuquan, Xixi, Huajiachi, Zhijiang, Zhoushan, International campus in Haining and Ningbo,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Zhejiang University encompasses an area of 6.22 square kilometers with school buildings covering 3.67 million square meters of floor space.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
#### Zijingang Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Zijingang Campus")]
Main article: [Zijingang Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zijingang_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Zijingang Campus, Zhejiang University")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/From_Linhu_Zijingang_ZJU.jpg/250px-From_Linhu_Zijingang_ZJU.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:From_Linhu_Zijingang_ZJU.jpg)[Zijingang Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zijingang_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Zijingang Campus, Zhejiang University"), the main campus of ZJU, which came into use in 2002
Zijingang campus serves as the main campus of Zhejiang University and is located in the northwest of Hangzhou. There are two libraries in the campus, i.e. the Basic Library next to the east gate and the Library of Agriculture and Medicine in the southeast corner and Library of Ancient Books in the south of the campus. The first floor of the Basic Library is an English corner every Tuesday and Thursday night.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:32-72) The campus is served by [Sanba Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanba_station "Sanba station") and [Xialongwei Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xialongwei_station "Xialongwei station") of the [Hangzhou Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Metro "Hangzhou Metro") to the east of the campus and [Zijingang Campus Zhejiang University Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zijingang_Campus_Zhejiang_University_station "Zijingang Campus Zhejiang University station") on the south side.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-73)
The South Gate of the campus is linked to the Zijingang Campus Zhejiang University station with bridges over the Yuhangtang River, which were opened in February 2022.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-74) The gigantic, five-arched South Gate was built with donations from alumni, but widely regarded unfit for the purpose among ZJU students.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-75) In a public poll in 2021, the South Gate was voted as the ugliest building in China.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-76)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-77)

#### Yuquan Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Yuquan Campus")]
Main article: [Yuquan Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuquan_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Yuquan Campus, Zhejiang University")
Zheda Road that stretches from the main gate of the campus to the [High School Attached to Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_School_Attached_to_Zhejiang_University "High School Attached to Zhejiang University") was known for its road greening landscape design.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-79) Alongside the road is a [compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microdistrict "Microdistrict") named Zheda Qiushi Village, also known as Qiushi Village, which was the residential area for Zhejiang University faculty and their family. Qiushi Primary School, also known as the Primary School Attached to Zhejiang University, and Hangzhou No. 15 Middle School, also known as the Junior High School Attached to Zhejiang University, are located near the compound.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-80) The Yuquan 1897 cafe within the campus is an [English corner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Corner "English Corner") every Wednesday evening.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:32-72)
#### Xixi Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Xixi Campus")]
Main article: [Xixi Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xixi_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Xixi Campus, Zhejiang University")
Xixi campus was previously the site of the former Hangzhou University before it merged into Zhejiang University in 1998. The campus hosts Department of Psychology and Behavioral Sciences, School of Art and Archaeology, and Zhejiang University Press. The library is located in the Center of campus. Between the library and the south gate of the campus is a large meadow. The campus is next to Xuejun High School. Xuejun used to be the affiliated high school of Hangzhou University, and is among top two high schools in Hangzhou, hence a major source of students admitted into Zhejiang University. Due to the location, the university canteen at Xixi was often overloaded with high school students.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-81)
#### Huajiachi Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Huajiachi Campus")]
Main article: [Huajiachi Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huajiachi_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Huajiachi Campus, Zhejiang University")
The Huajiachi campus was previously Zhejiang Agricultural University before merging with Zhejiang University and served as the old Huajiachi Campus for the National Chekiang University before the early 1950s.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:29-62) The campus is home to the departments of dentistry and agriculture, plus the College of Continuing Education. The Huajiachi campus is Zhejiang University's oldest campus. The Huajiachi initially refers to a lake within the campus, hence the name of the campus. The library is located on the east shore of the Huajiachi. The university made a plan to move out from the campus in 2007. As part of the plan, one fourth of the campus had been sold in 2013. In the plan, the campus will be transformed into a lakeside park that reserves most of the campus' old buildings.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:29-62)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-82)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Hangchow_University%2C_2018-10-28_04.jpg/250px-Hangchow_University%2C_2018-10-28_04.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hangchow_University,_2018-10-28_04.jpg)The Bell Tower of Zhijiang Campus was donated by [Shi Liangcai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shi_Liangcai "Shi Liangcai"), whose son studied at the campus in the 1930s. The building is now home to the Institute for Advanced Study in Humanities and Social Sciences.
#### Zhijiang Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Zhijiang Campus")]
Main article: [Zhijiang Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhijiang_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Zhijiang Campus, Zhejiang University")
The Zhijiang campus ([simplified Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): ; [traditional Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): ) is home to Guanghua Law School. Before being acquired by Zhejiang University in 1952, the Zhijiang campus served as the main campus of [Hangchow University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangchow_University "Hangchow University"), and is located on the Yuelun Hill next to the Qiantang River and the [Liuhe Pagoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liuhe_Pagoda "Liuhe Pagoda"). The campus is now home to James D. Watson Institute of Genome Sciences, [Guanghua Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guanghua_Law_School,_Zhejiang_University "Guanghua Law School, Zhejiang University") and the [Institute for Advanced Study in Humanities and Social Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institute_for_Advanced_Study_in_Humanities_and_Social_Sciences,_Zhejiang_University?action=edit&redlink=1 "Institute for Advanced Study in Humanities and Social Sciences, Zhejiang University \(page does not exist\)").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:28-83) The Library of Guanghua Law School is located to the north of the Main Teaching Building. Several buildings in the campus are listed as the [Major Historical and Cultural Sites Protected at the National Level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_Historical_and_Cultural_Site_Protected_at_the_National_Level "Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:28-83) The 2010 movie _[Aftershock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aftershock_\(2010_film\) "Aftershock \(2010 film\)")_ made the campus a popular tourist destination within the city, as the movie was shot on location within the campus to mimic a Chinese university life in the 1980s.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:28-83)

#### Zhoushan Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Zhoushan Campus")]
Zhoushan campus ([simplified Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters "Simplified Chinese characters"): ; [traditional Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_characters "Traditional Chinese characters"): ) is a campus that opened in 2015 and serves as the campus for the [Ocean College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean_College,_Zhejiang_University "Ocean College, Zhejiang University"). It is located in Lincheng, [Dinghai District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinghai_District "Dinghai District"), [Zhoushan City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhoushan "Zhoushan") on the [Zhoushan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhoushan_Island "Zhoushan Island").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:33-84) The Library of the Ocean College is located in the north of the campus. Between the library and the south gate is a meadow. The university's only training ship, named Zijingang, is deployed at the campus.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-85) Only third-year and fourth-year undergraduate students of the Ocean College and postgraduate students studied at the campus, while first-year and second-year students of the college receive education at Zijingang before moving to the campus in their third year.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:33-84)
#### Haining International Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Haining International Campus")]
Main article: [International Campus, Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "International Campus, Zhejiang University")
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Qiushi_Auditorium_at_Haining_Campus%2C_ZJU.jpg/250px-Qiushi_Auditorium_at_Haining_Campus%2C_ZJU.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Qiushi_Auditorium_at_Haining_Campus,_ZJU.jpg)Qiushi Auditorium at the Center of Haining Campus
Haining International Campus () is located in the Zhejiang city of [Haining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haining_\(city\) "Haining \(city\)").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-86) Clusters of international cooperative partners and institutions reside at this campus, which opened in 2016 as part of Zhejiang University.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:15-57)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:16-58) Student studying at the campus are also enrolled in the [residential college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residential_college "Residential college"). The first [master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_\(college\) "Master \(college\)") of the college is Professor [Lap-Chee Tsui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lap-Chee_Tsui "Lap-Chee Tsui").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-87)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-88)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-89) The International Campus Library is a three-storey octagonal building located on the northeast shore of the central lake of the campus.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-90) The campus is served by International Campus, ZJU station of [Hangzhou–Haining intercity railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou%E2%80%93Haining_intercity_railway "Hangzhou–Haining intercity railway"),[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-91) which opened on June 28, 2021.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-92)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-93)
Zhejiang University International Business School (ZIBS),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-94)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:30-95) the [Zhejiang University-University of Edinburgh Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University-University_of_Edinburgh_Institute "Zhejiang University-University of Edinburgh Institute") (ZJE),[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-96)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:30-95) the Zhejiang University–University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign Institute (ZJUI) and the [Imperial College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imperial_College_London "Imperial College London")-Zhejiang University Joint Applied Data Science Lab are located within the campus.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-97)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:30-95)
#### Ningbo Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Ningbo Campus")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/ZJUNIT_2020-06-04.jpg/250px-ZJUNIT_2020-06-04.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ZJUNIT_2020-06-04.jpg)The campus of NingboTech as well as ZJU's Ningbo Campus
The Ningbo campus was initiated as a collaboration with Ningbo city government in September 2017, with the campus' administration founded in September 2019. It was based on the campus of the former [Ningbo Institute of Technology (NIT) of Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NingboTech_University "NingboTech University") (now NingboTech University). Zhejiang University library has not set up a branch library in the campus, yet its resources are available at NingboTech's library. The campus is served by South Higher Education Park Station of [Ningbo Rail Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ningbo_Rail_Transit "Ningbo Rail Transit").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-98) The Polytechnic Institute of Zhejiang University started a branch in the campus since October 2016. Later, the Institute of Ningbo was founded in June 2018 within the campus of [Ningbo Institute of Technology (NIT), Zhejiang University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NingboTech_University "NingboTech University"). In January 2020, the NIT was made independent from Zhejiang University and renamed as NingboTech University, but remains in the campus. The campus is also home to the School of Software Technology, Zhejiang University.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-99)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-100)

During the Second World War, the university left its campus in Hangzhou to evade Japanese invasion. During the wartime relocation, the university also temporarily used the campuses in [Jiande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiande "Jiande") in 1937, [Ji'an](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ji'an "Ji'an"), [Taihe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taihe_County,_Jiangxi "Taihe County, Jiangxi") [Yishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yizhou_District,_Hechi "Yizhou District, Hechi") in 1938, before it finally arrived in [Meitan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meitan_County "Meitan County") and Zunyi, Guizhou in southwest China in early 1940. The university operated there for seven years until the war ended. In June 1939, the university set up a satellite campus headed by [Zheng Xiaocang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zheng_Xiaocang "Zheng Xiaocang") in [Longquan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longquan "Longquan"), Zhejiang.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-119)
In 2016, Dr. Ye Yongfei of the central committee of the [Revolutionary Committee of the Chinese Kuomintang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolutionary_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Kuomintang "Revolutionary Committee of the Chinese Kuomintang") suggest that the university restore the Meitan campus to support economic development in [western China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_China "Western China"), which was echoed by the local government of Zunyi who set up a committee to gather support in 2018. In March 2018, the university responded that it had no substantial plan to restore the Meitan campus.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-120)

### Motto
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Motto")]
During the University Council meeting held in [Yishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yizhou_District,_Hechi "Yizhou District, Hechi"), [Guangxi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guangxi "Guangxi") on November 19, 1938, "seeking truth" ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): ; [pinyin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin "Pinyin"): _Qiúshì_) was made the motto of the university, upon President Chu Kochen's advice. Qiushi is an excerpt of the famous quote in [Yangmingism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yangmingism "Yangmingism"), "A [Gentleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junzi "Junzi") learns only to know what is right. ([Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language"): )" It was made the name of the former body Qiushi Academy in 1897, which means seeking truth and has the same pronunciation as truth in English. According to Chu,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
> Seeking truth is not limited to studying hard or doing experiments in the lab. As [Doctrine of the Mean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctrine_of_the_Mean "Doctrine of the Mean") says, seeking truth is 'to study extensively, inquire prudently, think carefully, distinguish clearly, and practice earnestly.'
In May 1988, "pursuing innovation" was added to the university motto by the university council, to adapt the motto to the times of the [reform and opening up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reform_and_opening_up "Reform and opening up"). President [Lu Yongxiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Yongxiang_\(engineer\) "Lu Yongxiang \(engineer\)") explained in 1992,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
> Strictly speaking, pursuing innovation is included in seeking truth, [...] but people often regard seeking truth as being practical, emphasising the acknowledgement and application of the existing body of knowledge and the objective analysis and knowledge of the reality, with no emphasis on being creative and innovative.

### Quotes of Chu Kochen
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Quotes of Chu Kochen")]
[Chu Kochen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Coching "Chu Coching"), who served as the president of National Chekiang University from 1936 to 1949, is credited with a major impact on the guiding spirit of Zhejiang University.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-130) His two open questions for the freshmen who enrolled in 1936 has been inscribed in the stone next to the main gate of the [Zijingang Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zijingang_Campus,_Zhejiang_University "Zijingang Campus, Zhejiang University") as well as multiple sites within the university, which says,[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-131)
> You have two questions to ask yourself: First, what do you want to do at Zheda? Second, when you graduate, what kind of people do you want to be?
In another quote that is often displayed in the campus, Chu Kochen talks about the aim of university education, where he says,[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:37-132)
> The aim of university education is not to nurture experts such as engineers and doctors, but to build leaders that are just, patriotic, fortitudinous and persistent, that take major roles, that lead trends, and that change the destiny of this nation.
## Administration and organization
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Administration and organization")]
### Governance
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Governance")]
The university is organized according to Zhejiang University Chapter approved by the [Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Education_of_the_People's_Republic_of_China "Ministry of Education of the People's Republic of China"). The current chapter was approved in September 2014. According to the chapter, the university is a [national university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_university "National university") managed by the Ministry of Education and jointly funded by the central government and Zhejiang government. The university is operated by the Communist Party Committee of the university with the president taking the responsibility of decision making. The committee is required to ensure rule of law, academic freedom and democracy at the university.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:34-133) Since 2000, the president and [party secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Communist_Party_Committee_Secretary "Chinese Communist Party Committee Secretary") of the university are appointed by the [Organization Department of the Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organization_Department_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Organization Department of the Chinese Communist Party"), and the appointees are automatically considered as vice-ministerial level officials.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-134) The party committee elects the members of the standing committee, which decide major issues at the university jointly with the party committee. The president hosts university council meeting to decide on teaching and learning, scientific research and administrative issues. The faculty can review and advise on university decisions via the faculty representative meeting.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:34-133) The current party secretary of the university is Dr. Ren Shaobo. The president of the university is Professor Dr. Du Jiangfeng.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-135)
### Administrative departments
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Administrative departments")]
In the university has an administrative system that consists of 17 administrative departments. Among them, the Office of the Presidents set the strategic priorities for the university to maintain the university's leading position, while the Development and Planning Office is in charge of planning for the implementation of the strategic priorities. The Office of Global Engagement and the Division of Domestic Relations are responsible for implementing the university's strategy and promoting the university domestically and globally. The Human Resources Department recruits and provides services for the faculty, while the Undergraduate School and the Graduate School organise and supervise teaching, learning and degree awarding. The Administration of Continuing Education further provides training and supervision for continuing education programs. The research and development programs are supervised by the Sci-Tech Academy and the Academy of Humanities and Social Sciences, depending on the subject. The university research facilities and device are purchased, maintained, and evaluated by the Office of Laboratory and Equipment Management. The Department of General Affairs and the Office of Capital Construction are responsible for the management and construction of the university properties. The Medical Management Office manages the affiliated hospitals.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-136)

### Finances
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: Finances")]
According to the University Chapter, the university is largely funded by the government.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:34-133) The university has been selected into several national plans to nurture world-class universities, including [Double First-Class Construction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_First-Class_Construction "Double First-Class Construction"),[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-Chinese_Department_of_Education-143)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:1-144) [Project 985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_985 "Project 985") and [Project 211](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_211 "Project 211").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:26-145) In 2022, with a budget of 26.1 billion [Chinese yuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renminbi "Renminbi"), the university had the second largest budget in China after [Tsinghua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsinghua_University "Tsinghua University").[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-146) The university also raises money through income from its affiliations, government subsidy, donations and other legal sources of income.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:34-133) Zhejiang University consistently stands among top receivers of alumni donations in China. In 2021, it received 2.38 billion Chinese yuan, the fourth most after Tsinghua, Peking and Wuhan.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-147) On September 21, 2006, Chinese billionaires [Duan Yongping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duan_Yongping "Duan Yongping") (Zhejiang University [alumnus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alumnus "Alumnus")) and [Ding Lei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ding_Lei "Ding Lei") ([Zhejiang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang "Zhejiang") native) donated together a one-time [endowment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_endowment "Financial endowment") of 40 [million](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million "Million") US dollars to Zhejiang University. US$30 million was from Duan with 10 million from Ding. It was the largest private one-off endowment to a university in [Mainland China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainland_China "Mainland China").[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-148) In 2017, the university received a donation of 1.1 billion Chinese yuan (circa.160 million US dollars), again breaking the record for highest alumni donation.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-149)
## Academics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Academics")]
### Teaching and learning
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Teaching and learning")]
The academic departments are responsible for teaching and assessments of various courses and draft the details of degree programs, which needs to be approved by the Undergraduate and Graduate Schools before start; the detailed method may differ according to the course and the program. Teaching is supervised and regulated by the Undergraduate School and the Graduate School for quality control. [Chu Kochen Honors College (CKC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Kochen_Honors_College?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chu Kochen Honors College \(page does not exist\)"), named after the university's former president [Chu Kochen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chu_Coching "Chu Coching"), is an elite undergraduate college of ZJU, which further select students from top students at ZJU or in Gaokao.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-150)[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-151)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-152) Teaching at Chu Kochen Honors College and international dual degree programs at Haining are supervised and regulated by their own responsible committees.
Degree awarding is based on academic credits requirement for compulsory and elective courses, which a student must both fulfill to graduate. To earn academic credits, the student can choose and pass a combination of courses at his or her will, as long as the course is available for enrolment,[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-153) yet some courses may be competitive for enrolment due to class size limits.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-154)
#### Qiushi College
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Qiushi College")]
Qiushi College was founded in July 2008, as a residential college and part of the School of Undergraduate. It managed the student dormitories including the Danyang-Qingxi Hall, the Ziyun-Bifeng Hall, and the Lantian Hall. It offers liberal arts education for freshmen and supports student organizations and activities. It also provides students with aids for academic affairs such as college major choices and team building.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-155) Upon enrolment into the university, undergraduates join a hall of Qiushi College at Zijingang mostly according to their faculties of study. In the [student military training and education for all Chinese national freshmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_education_and_training_in_China "Military education and training in China"), the students are organized according to their halls within the college. In the first year of study, the major of the student may be unspecified as they are recruited according to academic faculties rather than specific academic subjects. They are considered to be a student of the Hall but not of an academic department then. The student may later apply to study a major later or transfer to another major during the study, yet the application to popular majors are highly competitive and additional requirements may apply. The college is responsible for providing assistance to the student.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-156)
#### Chu Kochen Honors College
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Chu Kochen Honors College")]
Chu Kochen Honors College (CKHC) was founded in May 2000 in honour of Chu Kochen, a former president of the university and is typically chaired by the current president of Zhejiang University. Its predecessor the Mixed Class of Engineering was launched in 1984. It offers a collection of programs including the Experimental Class of Engineering, the Mixed Class, the Experimental Class of Humanities and Social Sciences, the Qiushi Sciences Class, the Experimental Class of Medicine, the Shennong Class.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:35-157) Entry into the college is highly selective and competitive and its selection questions are known to be creative but difficult.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-158)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-159) Notable alumni of the college include entrepreneur [Colin Huang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colin_Huang "Colin Huang") and the current president of Zhejiang University [Wu Zhaohui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wu_Zhaohui "Wu Zhaohui").[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:35-157) Its teaching and learning are supervised by a special committee headed by the president. During the program, 15–20 percentile of the CKHC students in term of GPA will be transferred to non-CKHC programs.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:37-132)
#### International Campus
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: International Campus")]
The dual degree programs at the International Campus are supervised and regulated by the joint institute to fulfill academic requirements of both Zhejiang University and the partner institutes. For example, the University of Edinburgh regulations on progression and degree classification also applies to its joint institute at the campus, although they are not part of Zhejiang University regulations. The campus only provides a limited number of elective courses and allows students to elect a course that is not offered at his or her own institute. However, transfer from a Sino-foreign program to a purely ZJU program or between two programs of different joint institutes are not allowed. Transfer within the joint institute is allowed, yet its approval may be subject to the class size.
### Research
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=42 "Edit section: Research")]
Zhejiang University is a comprehensive research university. Research at Zhejiang University spans 12 academic disciplines: agriculture, art, economics, education, engineering, history, law, literature, management, medicine, natural sciences, and philosophy.
Among its approximate 4,191 standing faculty[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-160) members, more than 1,893 faculty members hold the title of professor. The faculty includes: 26 members of the [Chinese Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Sciences "Chinese Academy of Sciences"), 27 members of the [Chinese Academy of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Engineering "Chinese Academy of Engineering"), 164 [Chang Jiang (Yangtze River) Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Changjiang_Scholars_Program "Changjiang Scholars Program") winners, and 154 recipients of the awards from the National Science Fund for Distinguished Young Scholars. Zhejiang University also has prominent foreign faculty members. Zhejiang University has 11 [State Key Laboratories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Key_Laboratories "State Key Laboratories"), as one of the universities with most SKLs in China, which include:
  * Rice Biology, State Key Lab of
  * Chemical Engineering, State Key Lab of
  * Modern Optical Instrumentation, State Key Lab of
  * Industrial Control Technology, State Key Lab of
  * Fluid Power Transmission and Control, State Key Lab of
  * CAD and Computer Graphics, State Key Lab of
  * Diagnosis and Treatment of Infectious Diseases, State Key Lab of
  * Clean Energy Utilization, State Key Lab of
  * Silicon Materials, State Key Lab of
  * Plant Physiology and Biochemistry, State Key Lab of
  * Modern Optical Instrumentation, State Key Lab of


The university also has three State Specialized Labs, including the State Specialized Lab of Secondary Resources Chemical Engineering, the State Specialized Lab of Power Electronics, and the State Specialized Lab of Biomedical Sensor. Besides, the university has three labs of the Ministry of Education (MOE), including the MOE Key Lab of Soft Soils and Geoenvironmental Engineering, the MOE Key Lab of Conservation Genetics and Reproductive Biology for Endangered Wildlife and the MOE-Microsoft Key Lab of Visual Perception.
### Library system
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zhejiang_University&action=edit&section=43 "Edit section: Library system")]
The library system has a total library collection of more than 7.9 million volumes,[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-161) which is one of China's largest academic collections.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-162) The system has 6 branch libraries, namely Yuquan Campus Library, Basic Library of Zijingang Campus, Library of Agriculture and Medicine of Zijingang Campus, Library of Ancient Books of Zijingang Campus,[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-163) Xixi Campus Library and Hujiachi Campus Library,[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:36-164) plus 3 branch libraries within different colleges, namely Guanghua Law School Library, International Campus Library, Ocean College Library.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-165) Zijingang Campus is the only campus to have three library.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-:36-164) One can reserve a book at any library for collection of a book that may belong to another library in the system.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhejiang_University#cite_note-166)
